title: Proof-Carrying Numbers: checking every figure in an AI answer against its data
description: An AI chatbot that answers from statistics can write a figure that differs from its source, and a reader cannot tell this from the text of the answer. This video explains Proof-Carrying Numbers (PCN), a method that links each figure in an answer to the record it came from and checks the figure against that record before the reader sees it.

The example uses internet use in Kenya and Rwanda from the World Bank's World Development Indicators. The video follows the data as each value receives a claim id, the instructions that ask the model to tag every figure, the answer with its tags, the verifier that checks each tag in ordinary code, and the marks that a reader sees in the chatbot. A verified mark says that a figure matches its record. Whether that record answers the question remains the reader's judgement.
chapters: The data and its claim ids
about: Data: World Bank, World Development Indicators, indicator IT.NET.USER.ZS (Individuals using the Internet, % of population), from api.worldbank.org, last updated 8 October 2026. CC BY 4.0.
The chatbot answer is an example written for this video. The narration is read by a synthetic voice (Kokoro text-to-speech).
AI for Data – Data for AI, World Bank: https://worldbank.github.io/ai4data/
